title: Expression values and notifications
summary: String and direct Observable expressions, formState observation and expression change event payloads.

facts.claim: Formly string expressions are evaluated with model, formState and field bindings.
conditions: An expression value is a string in Formly 6.3.12.
limits: This is distinct from the modern expressions function callback, whose public argument is the field.
This does not establish a security sandbox for untrusted expression text.
facts.context: String expression names such as model.label, formState.mode and field.key; not the legacy function callback signature.
facts.source_quote:
| API | Relevant contract |
| --- | --- |
| `expressions: { 'props.disabled': fn }` | Public callback receives the field; read `field.model` and `field.options.formState` |
| Legacy `expressionProperties` / `hideExpression` function | Model, formState, optional field arguments |
| String expression | Evaluated with model, formState, field bindings |
| Observable expression | Value stream applied to the targeted field property |

Evidence: declarations [K01](sources.md#k01), evaluator [K07](sources.md#k07), tests [K25](sources.md#k25). One upstream test title still mentions the older arguments, but its assertion checks a field argument. Prefer declarations and assertions over the test title. An extra internal evaluation flag is not a reason to build application callbacks around undocumented arguments.

facts.claim: An Observable assigned directly as an expression value supplies values to the targeted field property.
conditions: The expressions map contains the Observable itself as the value, for example expressions["props.label"].
limits: Do not infer the same subscription contract for a function callback returning an Observable.
This expression value stream is distinct from select options streams and managed onInit hook returns.
facts.context: Using an Observable directly for an expression target versus returning a stream from an expressions function.

facts.claim: The Formly 6.3.12 form component observes changes to formState and calls detectChanges.
conditions: The pinned Formly 6.3.12 form component observation path.
limits: Patch-sensitive behavior is not a universal guarantee for every mutation, environment or Formly version.
The default checkExpressionOn modelChange setting does not justify saying formState changes are never detected.
facts.context: formState notification and expression reevaluation under the default modelChange setting.
facts.source_quote: The default is `checkExpressionOn: 'modelChange'`. v6.3.12 also observes changes to formState in the form component and calls detectChanges. That detail is patch-sensitive; avoid old blanket advice that formState changes are never detected [K04](sources.md#k04), [K11](sources.md#k11), [K29](sources.md#k29).

facts.claim: options.fieldChanges emits expressionChanges events containing field, property and value; property identifies the actual expression target path.
conditions: The expression evaluator emits an expressionChanges notification through options.fieldChanges.
limits: Do not promise a notification on every evaluation; function/string evaluation is cached.
Filter the event type and actual property path rather than treating every fieldChanges notification as the same event.
facts.context: Observe expression updates; event.type expressionChanges, event.field, event.property and event.value; props.disabled and templateOptions.disabled remain distinct paths.
facts.source_quote: `options.checkExpressions(field)` evaluates expressions; `options.detectChanges(field)` invokes expression checks and marks the relevant components. These operations do not replace inspecting the root cause of an update problem [K05](sources.md#k05), [K07](sources.md#k07). `options.fieldChanges` includes events with type `expressionChanges`, property, field, and value; filter them for the actual dependency [K07](sources.md#k07).
